group.title: Entertainment
sources: Words and CEFR levels chosen by the authors from general knowledge of English; meanings, examples and sentences are original

Word-list licences checked 2026-10-25: CEFR-J Wordlist 1.5 (Tono Laboratory, TUFS; free with citation, A1-B2) and NGSL/NAWL (CC BY-SA 4.0) were not copied; Oxford 3000 and English Vocabulary Profile terms were not confirmed, so they were not used

words.meaning: A story told with moving pictures and sound.
examples: Let’s watch a {movie} tonight.
wrong: I read a movie with no pictures in bed.

words.meaning: A building where you pay to watch films on a big screen.
examples: We saw the new film at the {cinema}.
wrong: I watched the film at the cinema on my small phone at home.

words.meaning: Made with drawings or computer pictures that seem to move.
examples: Kids love {animated} films with talking animals.
wrong: The animated film used only real actors and no drawings.

words.meaning: Loud popular music with electric guitars and drums.
examples: He plays {rock music} in his garage.
wrong: Rock music is soft and quiet, played on a harp.

words.meaning: A famous singer of popular music.
examples: The {pop star} sang her new song on TV.
wrong: The pop star has never sung in public.

words.meaning: A very famous film actor.
examples: A {movie star} visited our town and everyone wanted a photo.
wrong: Nobody knows the movie star’s name.

words.meaning: A character in a story with special powers who saves people.
examples: The {superhero} can fly faster than a plane.
wrong: The superhero has no powers and never helps anyone.

words.meaning: A group of people who play music together.
examples: My brother plays guitar in a {band}.
wrong: The band was just one person reading a book.

words.meaning: A collection of songs that come out together.
examples: Her new {album} has twelve songs.
wrong: An album is one short note of music.

words.meaning: A short film made to go with a song.
examples: The {music video} was filmed on a beach.
wrong: A music video has no music in it.

words.meaning: Modern, popular songs that are easy to listen to.
examples: She listens to {pop music} on the radio.
wrong: Pop music is very old and nobody likes it.

words.meaning: Describing serious music written long ago, often for orchestras.
examples: He listens to {classical} music when he studies.
wrong: Classical music was written last week by a rock band.

words.meaning: A kind of music with a strong rhythm, often made up while playing.
examples: They play {jazz} at the café on Friday nights.
wrong: Jazz is a sport played with a ball.

words.meaning: Instruments you hit with sticks to make a beat.
examples: He plays the {drums} very loudly.
wrong: She plays the drums by blowing into them.

words.meaning: A film or book about two people falling in love.
examples: My sister cried at the end of the {love story}.
wrong: The love story was about soldiers who hated each other.

words.meaning: Stories about the future, space or new technology.
examples: She loves {science fiction} films about space.
wrong: Science fiction is true stories about the past.

words.meaning: A program you watch on television.
examples: My favorite {TV show} is on at eight.
wrong: I listened to the TV show on paper.

words.meaning: A program where a host chats with famous guests.
examples: The singer was a guest on a {talk show}.
wrong: On the talk show, nobody said a word.

words.meaning: A program where people answer questions or play to win prizes.
examples: He won a car on a {game show}.
wrong: In a game show, there are no games and no prizes.

words.meaning: A set of programs with the same characters, shown one after another.
examples: I watched the whole {series} in one weekend.
wrong: The series had only one show and nothing more.

words.meaning: A small device you use to change the channel from your seat.
examples: Where’s the {remote control}? I want to change the channel.
wrong: I opened the door of the house with the TV remote control.

words.meaning: A film or show made with drawings.
examples: The kids watch {cartoons} on Saturday morning.
wrong: The cartoon used only real people and no drawings.

words.meaning: A film or show that makes people laugh.
examples: We watched a {comedy} and laughed all night.
wrong: The comedy was so sad that everyone cried.

words.meaning: A film with lots of fights, chases and excitement.
examples: The {action movie} had car chases and explosions.
wrong: The action movie was quiet and slow, with nothing happening.

words.meaning: A serious film, play or show about people’s lives.
examples: The {drama} is about a family with a big secret.
wrong: The drama was full of jokes and silly songs.

words.meaning: A TV series about the daily lives of a group of people, shown often.
examples: My grandma watches a {soap opera} every afternoon.
wrong: The soap opera is a show about washing clothes.

words.meaning: A TV program that films real people, not actors.
examples: She was on a {reality show} about cooking.
wrong: The reality show used actors reading a script.

words.meaning: The main good character in a story or film.
examples: The {hero} saves the city at the end.
wrong: The hero is the bad man who causes all the trouble.

words.meaning: The bad character in a story or film.
examples: The {villain} wants to steal the gold.
wrong: The villain is the kind man who helps everyone.

words.meaning: The last part of a story or film.
examples: The film has a happy {ending}.
wrong: The ending is at the very start of the book.

words.meaning: Corn that pops when it is heated, often eaten at the cinema.
examples: We shared a big bag of {popcorn} during the film.
wrong: I drank a cup of popcorn.

words.meaning: A person who introduces a TV or radio program.
examples: The {presenter} welcomed the guests to the show.
wrong: The presenter never speaks on the show.

words.meaning: A play or film where the story is told with songs and dancing.
examples: We saw a {musical} in the theater.
wrong: The musical had no music at all.

words.meaning: A person who watches a TV program.
examples: Millions of {viewers} watched the final.
wrong: The viewers never watch TV.

words.meaning: To hit your hands together to show you liked something.
examples: Everyone {clapped} at the end of the show.
wrong: The audience clapped because they hated the show.

words.meaning: Making you feel very interested and full of energy.
examples: The match was so {exciting}!
wrong: The film was so exciting that I fell asleep.

words.meaning: Music that people play in front of you, not a recording.
examples: The café has {live music} every Friday.
wrong: The live music came from an old recording.

words.meaning: Special clothes an actor wears to look like a character.
examples: The actor wore a pirate {costume}.
wrong: A costume is the money you pay for a ticket.

words.meaning: A song or film that is very popular.
examples: The song was a big {hit} last summer.
wrong: The song was a hit, so nobody bought it.

words.meaning: Tricks used to make impossible things look real in a film.
examples: The {special effects} made the dragon look real.
wrong: The film has special effects, so everything looks fake.
